topic: Algebra II - Complex Numbers & Binomial Theorem

sections.title: Polar and Euler Form
sections.content: A complex number z = a + ib can be written in polar form as r(cosθ + i sinθ) or Euler form as r*e^(iθ), where r = |z| and θ is the principal argument of z.

sections.title: Cube Roots of Unity
sections.content: The solutions to z³ = 1 are 1, ω, and ω². They represent the vertices of an equilateral triangle on the Argand plane. Crucial properties: 1 + ω + ω² = 0 and ω³ = 1.

sections.title: Properties of Modulus and Conjugate
sections.content: Important rules: |z1 * z2| = |z1| * |z2|, (z1/z2)* = z1* / z2*, and z * z* = |z|². The triangle inequality states |z1 + z2| ≤ |z1| + |z2|.

sections.title: Square Root of a Complex Number
sections.content: The square root of (a + ib) yields two complex numbers: ±[√((|z|+a)/2) + i * sign(b) * √((|z|-a)/2)].

sections.title: Properties of Binomial Coefficients
sections.content: Let nCr be denoted as Cr. Standard properties include C0 + C1 + ... + Cn = 2^n, and C0 - C1 + C2 - ... = 0. Also, nCr = nC(n-r).

sections.title: Numerically Greatest Term (NGT)
sections.content: To find the largest term in (1+x)^n, calculate m = |x(n+1) / (x+1)|. If m is an integer, both Tm and T(m+1) are greatest. If fractional, T([m]+1) is the greatest.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Miscalculating the principal argument θ (it must lie in (-π, π]).
2) Forgetting the sign of 'b' when finding the square root of a complex number.
3) Applying basic properties without checking if n is even/odd in series summations.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 shifts to geometrical forms (Euler/Polar), special roots (cube roots of unity), bounding using triangle inequality, and manipulating binomial coefficient series.

tricks.title: The (1±i) Trick
tricks.explanation: Squaring (1+i) or (1-i) simplifies immediately to pure imaginary numbers.

tricks.title: Omega Reduction
tricks.explanation: Reduce large powers of ω by dividing the exponent by 3, similar to powers of i.

tricks.title: Sum of Even/Odd Binomial Coefficients
tricks.explanation: The sum of only even or only odd positioned coefficients is exactly half of the total sum.

tricks.title: Ratio of Consecutive Coefficients
tricks.explanation: The ratio nCr / nC(r-1) simplifies to a very useful fraction to avoid factorial expansion.

tricks.title: Modulus Triangle Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Use triangle inequalities to quickly find the maximum or minimum distance/modulus without solving.
tricks.example: Min value of |z - 3| + |z - 5| occurs on the line segment between 3 and 5, which is |5 - 3| = 2.

tricks.title: Index Shifting in Binomial Products
tricks.explanation: For sums like Σ (nCr * nC(r+k)), the result is exactly 2nC(n-k).
